opening.text: A car has a steering wheel for a reason. The driver does not control the road. But the driver does choose where to turn. One small turn of the wheel, held for a mile, takes the car to a very different place.
Young people hold a steering wheel too. They cannot control everything around them. But their choices decide where they head.

mainMessage.text: The power to choose is a gift from God. Young people are not left to steer alone. Jesus Christ is the best guide they can have, and He is their strength.

blocks.text: **Pick a guide.** A good driver checks the map. A wise young person checks with the Savior. He knows the road, and He has walked it Himself.
And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
To be very clear, the best guide you can possibly have for making choices is Jesus Christ.
He is the best guide.
**The wheel is yours.** Nobody else can turn your wheel. God gave each of us the power to choose. It is at the heart of His plan for our happiness.

Wherefore, men are free according to the flesh; and all things are given them which are expedient unto man. And they are free to choose liberty and eternal life, through the great Mediator of all men, or to choose captivity and death, according to the captivity and power of the devil; for he seeketh that all men might be miserable like unto himself.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
At the heart of God’s plan for your happiness is your power to choose.
The choice is yours.
**Trust the One who sees the road.** A driver cannot see around every curve. We cannot see where each choice leads. But we can trust the One who can.
Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Put your trust in Jesus Christ.
We trust the One who sees ahead.
**Learn the road early.** A young driver learns the rules before the first big trip. Young people who learn to keep the commandments early find the road much easier later on.
O, remember, my son, and learn wisdom in thy youth; yea, learn in thy youth to keep the commandments of God.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
He will lead you the right way.
He leads the right way.
**When the engine sputters.** Every driver has a day when things go wrong. Young people feel weak sometimes too. In those moments, the Savior is their strength.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
When you feel weak, Jesus Christ is your strength.
When we are weak, He is strong.
**Not driving alone.** Young people do not make their choices in a vacuum. They have friends, family and leaders alongside them. Together, they can travel farther.

Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone? And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Brother Steven J. Lund, Young Men General President, said this about the youth of Zion in his talk “Lasting Discipleship” from the October 2022 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Thankfully, they do not have to go out into battle alone.
They are not alone.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they made a good choice as a young person, or helped a young person make one. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Daniel Purposes in His Heart

blocks.text: Daniel was a young man far from home, in a place where everyone around him did things differently. He made up his mind early.

But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
Daniel decided before the test came. That is a wise way to choose.

application.text: First, think of one choice you face this week. Ask yourself, “What would Jesus Christ want me to do?”
Second, decide now, before the moment comes. Tell a trusted friend or family member.
Third, if a choice feels too big to make alone, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God gave us the power to choose. I know that Jesus Christ will guide us when we ask Him. I have felt His strength when I felt weak. I know that He loves every young person. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to think of one choice you face this week and ask, "What would Jesus Christ want me to do?"
I invite you to decide now, before the moment comes, and tell a trusted friend or family member.
I invite you to speak with your bishop or branch president if a choice feels too big to make alone.
blessings: You will make choices with confidence.
You will be held to your goals.

closingVerse.text: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.

opening.text: A hiker comes to a fork in the trail. One path goes up through the trees. The other goes down toward the stream. Both look fine. The map is not clear. The hiker has to choose. Then, a mile later, the choice shows.
Life puts forks in front of young people all the time. Most of them look small. But they add up.

mainMessage.text: Every young person has the power to choose. They do not have to pick the path without help. Jesus Christ is the surest guide and the strength for every step.

blocks.text: **Ask the guide.** A smart hiker asks someone who knows the trail. A wise young person asks the Savior. He knows where each path leads.
And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
To be very clear, the best guide you can possibly have for making choices is Jesus Christ.
He knows each path.
**The fork is yours.** No one can choose for you. The power to choose is a gift, and it is at the heart of God’s plan for our happiness.

Wherefore, men are free according to the flesh; and all things are given them which are expedient unto man. And they are free to choose liberty and eternal life, through the great Mediator of all men, or to choose captivity and death, according to the captivity and power of the devil; for he seeketh that all men might be miserable like unto himself.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
At the heart of God’s plan for your happiness is your power to choose.
The fork is yours to choose.
**Lean on Him.** On a steep trail, a good walking stick helps. Trust in the Lord is a support that does not fail. We do not need to rely only on our own understanding.
Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Put your trust in Jesus Christ.
We lean on Him.
**Start the hike early.** The earlier a hiker learns to read the signs, the safer every future hike will be. The same is true of learning the commandments in youth.
O, remember, my son, and learn wisdom in thy youth; yea, learn in thy youth to keep the commandments of God.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
He will lead you the right way.
He leads us right.
**Tired legs.** Every hiker gets tired. Young people get tired too, and they feel weak sometimes. The Savior gives strength when ours runs out.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
When you feel weak, Jesus Christ is your strength.
His strength lasts when ours ends.
**A hiking party.** Hikers go in groups for safety. Young people do not walk their path alone. They have each other, and they have leaders who care.

Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone? And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Brother Steven J. Lund, Young Men General President, said this about the youth of Zion in his talk “Lasting Discipleship” from the October 2022 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Thankfully, they do not have to go out into battle alone.
They walk together.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a hard choice shaped the path they took. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: David Trusts the Lord

blocks.text: David was a young shepherd. When a giant threatened Israel, he did not look at the size of the giant. He remembered how the Lord had helped him before.

David said moreover, The Lord that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said unto David, Go, and the Lord be with thee.
David chose to trust, and the Lord was with him.

application.text: First, write down two choices you will face this week. Next to each, write what a disciple of Jesus Christ would choose.
Second, share one of them with a friend who can help you stay true.
Third, if a choice is weighing on you, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that Jesus Christ knows every path we face. I know that He gives strength to those who ask. I have felt His guidance in my own choices. I know that every young person can find their way with Him. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to write down two choices you will face this week and what a disciple of Jesus Christ would choose.
I invite you to share one with a friend who can help you stay true.
I invite you to speak with your bishop or branch president if a choice is weighing on you.
blessings: You will see your path clearly.

closingVerse.text: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.

opening.text: A big ship has a small part at the back called the rudder. It is tiny compared with the ship. But a small turn of the rudder, held steady, sets the whole ship on a new course. After a hundred miles, the ship is somewhere very different.
Young people have a rudder too. Their daily choices are small. But they add up to a direction.

mainMessage.text: Each choice is a small turn of the rudder. God gave young people the power to make them. Jesus Christ is the best guide and the strength to hold steady.

blocks.text: **Who sets the course.** A captain reads the chart and follows a lighthouse. A young person can follow the Savior. He is the best guide for any choice.
And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
To be very clear, the best guide you can possibly have for making choices is Jesus Christ.
He sets the true course.
**The hand on the rudder.** It is your hand. The power to choose is a gift, and it is at the heart of God’s plan for our happiness.

Wherefore, men are free according to the flesh; and all things are given them which are expedient unto man. And they are free to choose liberty and eternal life, through the great Mediator of all men, or to choose captivity and death, according to the captivity and power of the devil; for he seeketh that all men might be miserable like unto himself.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
At the heart of God’s plan for your happiness is your power to choose.
The hand is yours.
**Trust the chart.** A captain trusts a good chart even in fog. Trust in the Lord works the same way. When we cannot see ahead, we can still trust the One who can.
Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Put your trust in Jesus Christ.
We trust the chart in the fog.
**Set the course early.** The sooner a ship is pointed right, the less it has to correct. Learning to keep the commandments in youth is the same. It saves a lot of sorrow later.
O, remember, my son, and learn wisdom in thy youth; yea, learn in thy youth to keep the commandments of God.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
He will lead you the right way.
He will lead the right way.
**Rough seas.** Even a good captain meets storms. Young people feel weak sometimes. When they do, the Savior is the strength they can lean on.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
When you feel weak, Jesus Christ is your strength.
His strength rides the storm.
**A crew.** No captain sails alone. A crew works together. Young people have each other and leaders who care. They are not alone at sea.

Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone? And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Brother Steven J. Lund, Young Men General President, said this about the youth of Zion in his talk “Lasting Discipleship” from the October 2022 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Thankfully, they do not have to go out into battle alone.
The crew sails together.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a small choice led somewhere much bigger. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jesus Grows in Wisdom

blocks.text: Jesus grew up as a young person like others. The scripture tells us how He grew.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.
He grew step by step, in wisdom, in body and in goodness. Young people can grow the same way.

application.text: First, name one small choice you make daily that sets your direction, such as how you spend your first minutes in the morning.
Second, turn it a little toward the Savior this week.
Third, if you feel off course, speak with your bishop or branch president. They will help you set it right.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that small, steady choices can change a life. I know that Jesus Christ helps us hold the course. I have seen young people grow strong in Him. I know that He is the Strength of youth. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to name one small daily choice that sets your direction.
I invite you to turn it a little toward the Savior this week.
I invite you to speak with your bishop or branch president if you feel off course.
blessings: You will move in a better direction.
You will feel the Savior near.
You will be helped back on course.

closingVerse.text: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.

opening.text: Before a climber steps onto a steep wall, she puts on a harness and checks the rope. She picks the route and she does the climbing. But she is not alone. A partner holds the other end and watches every move.
Choices can feel like climbing. They are yours to make. But you do not have to make them without support.

mainMessage.text: Young people do the climbing. God gave them the power to choose. And Jesus Christ is the rope, the guide and the strength all at once.

blocks.text: **The best route.** A climber studies the wall and asks an experienced guide. The Savior is the best guide a young person can have for making choices.
And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
To be very clear, the best guide you can possibly have for making choices is Jesus Christ.
He knows the best route.
**Your hands, your grip.** Nobody can climb the wall for you. The power to choose is your own. It is at the heart of God’s plan for your happiness.

Wherefore, men are free according to the flesh; and all things are given them which are expedient unto man. And they are free to choose liberty and eternal life, through the great Mediator of all men, or to choose captivity and death, according to the captivity and power of the devil; for he seeketh that all men might be miserable like unto himself.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
At the heart of God’s plan for your happiness is your power to choose.
The climb is yours.
**Trust the rope.** A climber who does not trust the rope cannot climb well. When we put our trust in Jesus Christ, we can reach higher than we could alone.
Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Put your trust in Jesus Christ.
The rope holds when we trust it.
**Learn the skills early.** Climbers practice basic skills on easy walls first. Youth is a good time to learn the commandments. The skills are ready when the hard wall comes.
O, remember, my son, and learn wisdom in thy youth; yea, learn in thy youth to keep the commandments of God.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
He will lead you the right way.
He leads us up the right way.
**Shaky arms.** Every climber’s arms shake near the top. We all feel weak at times. The Savior’s strength starts where ours runs out.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
When you feel weak, Jesus Christ is your strength.
He holds us when we shake.
**The partner on the ground.** The person who holds the other end of the rope is part of every climb. Young people have friends, family and leaders who hold the rope for them.

Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone? And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Brother Steven J. Lund, Young Men General President, said this about the youth of Zion in his talk “Lasting Discipleship” from the October 2022 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Thankfully, they do not have to go out into battle alone.
Someone holds the rope.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a friend, parent or leader helped them stay strong in a hard choice. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The Young Warriors

blocks.text: The sons of Helaman were young men who faced real danger. What made them strong was what they had been taught.

And they were all young men, and they were exceedingly valiant for courage, and also for strength and activity; but behold, this was not all—they were men who were true at all times in whatsoever thing they were entrusted. Yea, they were men of truth and soberness, for they had been taught to keep the commandments of God and to walk uprightly before him.
They chose well because they had been taught well, and they stood together.

application.text: First, think of one friend who helps you choose well. Thank them in person or by message.
Second, be that kind of friend for someone else this week.
Third, if you need an adult you can trust, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that young people can do hard things with the Savior’s help. I know that good friends and leaders are a gift from God. I have felt the strength of being held up. I know that Jesus Christ never lets go of those who hold on to Him. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to thank one friend who helps you choose well.
I invite you to be that kind of friend for someone else this week.
I invite you to speak with a trusted adult, such as your bishop or branch president, when you need help.
blessings: Someone will be lifted by you.

closingVerse.text: Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.

opening.text: To cross a stream, you step from stone to stone. You do not leap the whole way. You choose one stone, test it and step. Then you choose the next. The stones are not always where you expect. But if you take them one at a time, you get across.
Choices in youth are like that. One step at a time.

mainMessage.text: A young person crosses life one choice at a time. God gave them the power to choose. And Jesus Christ is the guide who shows the next stone and the strength to take the step.

blocks.text: **Ask which stone.** A good guide points to the safe stone. The Savior points the way for each choice. He is the best guide a young person can have.
And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
To be very clear, the best guide you can possibly have for making choices is Jesus Christ.
He points to the safe stone.
**The step is yours.** Another person can point, but only you can step. The power to choose is a gift. It is at the heart of God’s plan for your happiness.

Wherefore, men are free according to the flesh; and all things are given them which are expedient unto man. And they are free to choose liberty and eternal life, through the great Mediator of all men, or to choose captivity and death, according to the captivity and power of the devil; for he seeketh that all men might be miserable like unto himself.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
At the heart of God’s plan for your happiness is your power to choose.
The step is yours to take.
**Test your weight on it.** You trust a stone before you stand on it. You can trust the Lord the same way. He has proven worthy of trust.
Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Put your trust in Jesus Christ.
We test our weight on Him.
**Learn to read the stream.** People who learn early to read moving water cross more safely. Learning the commandments in youth helps young people see the safe path.
O, remember, my son, and learn wisdom in thy youth; yea, learn in thy youth to keep the commandments of God.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
He will lead you the right way.
He leads across the right way.
**When your foot slips.** Sometimes a stone is slick. A foot slips. We all slip. The Savior is there to steady us.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Jesus Christ Is the Strength of Youth” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
When you feel weak, Jesus Christ is your strength.
He steadies us when we slip.
**A hand across the gap.** Crossing is easier when someone reaches out a hand. Young people have friends and leaders who do that. They do not cross alone.

Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone? And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Brother Steven J. Lund, Young Men General President, said this about the youth of Zion in his talk “Lasting Discipleship” from the October 2022 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Thankfully, they do not have to go out into battle alone.
A hand reaches across.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone young led by example. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Paul Encourages Young Timothy

blocks.text: Timothy was a young leader. Some may have thought he was too young. Paul gave him a clear way to answer them.
Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
Youth is not a reason to wait. Young people can lead by how they live.

application.text: First, ask yourself where you can be an example this week, in what you say, how you treat people or how you stay pure.
Second, pick one thing to do, and do it.
Third, if you want help setting good goals, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that young people can make a big difference. I know that Jesus Christ helps them choose well. I have seen youth lead by example. I know that He is their strength and mine. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to think of where you can be an example this week in what you say, how you treat others or how you stay pure.
I invite you to pick one thing to do, and do it.
I invite you to speak with your bishop or branch president about setting good goals.
blessings: Others will be blessed by your example.
You will be guided toward your goals.

closingVerse.text: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
